title: Constant-module projection formula for a bounded torsion object over Noetherian coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $f:X\to Y$ a separated $k$-morphism between schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of small-etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the module-sheaf derived direct image $Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and uncompleted derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $E\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ have Tor amplitude in a finite interval $[u,v]$ for integers $u\leq v$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], and suppose $N\cdot\mathrm{id}_E=0$ for an integer $N\geq1$ invertible on $Y$. For every $\Lambda$-module $M$, with constant module sheaves $\underline M_X,\underline M_Y$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], the canonical counit-defined projection morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map]
$$
\mathrm{PF}_f(E,\underline M_Y):\quad
Rf_*E\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}\underline M_Y[0]
\longrightarrow Rf_*\bigl(E\otimes_\Lambda^{\mathbf L}\underline M_X[0]\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, natural in $E$ and $M$. No finite generation, finite presentation, flatness, or finite projective dimension of $M$ is assumed; $E$ need not be constructible.

source.place: Tag 0F12, lemma-pull-out-constant-mod-n, its direct-sum/triangle/unit argument adapted to relative direct image and a bounded torsion object over a possibly nontorsion Noetherian coefficient ring. proof.text: Finite-type schemes over k are locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, and X is quasi-compact. Thus f is qcqs. Apply torsionEtaleCohomologicalDimension_finite_of_finiteType to obtain cd(f) < infinity, using its relative clause only.

Let C = constantFunctor Lambda Y, L the derived inverse image, R the derived direct image, and T tensor with E. Whisker rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMapApp by C, giving tau from C followed by tensor with R(E) to (C followed by L followed by T) followed by R. The existing etale triangulated and shift instances make both functors exact and tau shift-compatible. This is the original module-sheaf projection mate. The existing isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMapApp_constantSingle_self proves invertibility at the degree-zero constant Lambda, from projection-unit normalization. Transport it across mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor to give invertibility of tau at Lambda[0].

source.place: rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMapApp, isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMapApp_constantSingle_self, isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMapApp_of_iso; ConstantTensorProjection.lean, preservesColimitsOfShape_constantFunctor; LowerShriekProjectionShift.lean shift instance; Triangulated.lean exactness instances.

proof.text: For every P, the additive functor tensoring on the right by P maps N id_E = 0 to N id_(E tensor P) = 0. For a family P_i in D(Lambda), set K_i = T(L(C(P_i))). Apply the fixed-exponent coproduct comparison theorem with the original Lambda, exponent N, and the relative bound of Step 1. PreservesCoproduct.of_iso_comparison turns its invertible sigmaComparison into preservation by R of this particular diagram. Constants preserve coproducts as an exact coproduct-preserving functor induced on derived categories; L preserves them by its adjunction, and tensor preserves them by the derived tensor coproduct theorem. The composite target therefore preserves the coproduct of P_i. The source preserves it for the same reason. No global coproduct-preservation assertion for R over arbitrary coefficients is made.

Apply derivedModuleFreeGeneration to the property IsIso(tau.app P). Step 2 and NatTrans.isIso_app_shift_iff give every shifted rank-one generator; identify ULift Lambda with Lambda via ULift.moduleEquiv. For a coproduct cofan, naturality and Step 3 give IsIso at its point by NatTrans.isIso_app_of_isColimit_cofan. The triangle-isomorphism theorem gives closure under third vertices, and NatTrans.isIso_app_of_retract gives retract closure. Hence tau is invertible at every P.

Evaluate at M[0]. The canonical mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor isomorphism identifies C(M[0]) with the degree-zero constant module sheaf. NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso then gives exactly the component of rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap in the theorem statement. No inverse-image constant-module bridge is needed because the stated target is already expressed using the existing derived inverse image. Naturality is inherited from that original transformation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-7fc364ded (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole split: Stacks 0F10, 0F11 and 0F12 (etale-cohomology.tex l.20015-20200, statements and proofs), 0D6J(3), and every cited node statement. 0F12 is absolute and needs a torsion ring; the item is an agent extension over any ring with torsion E, and its statement is kept, not weakened. The steps check out. Step 1: lem-kun-0f10(1) gives cd(f)<inf for a k-morphism of finite-type k-schemes, for all torsion sheaves. Step 2: lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact supplies exactness, shift compatibility, naturality and alpha=1 at the unit; this is the same mate as def-kun-projection-formula-map; c_Y is exact and a left adjoint. Step 3: coproducts pass through c_Y, f^{-1} and the tensor; then the new node with n=N, since N*id=0 passes through the tensor. Step 4: Lambda[j], third vertex by lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three, coproducts, and retracts (inverse F(r)alpha_Q^{-1}G(i), checked); lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation then covers all of D(Lambda). Step 5: lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module (any ring, any module) gives f^{-1}M_Y = M_X. New node lem-sf-fixed-exponent-derived-coproducts: statement only and self-contained, sources 0F11 and 0D6J by label, five searches. It is true: forget to Z via 0D6J(3); A tensor^L Z/n = Cone(n) = A + A[1] when n=0 on A, so A is a retract of an object over Z/n where 0F11(1) applies. Small cases checked: Lambda=Q, Lambda=Z/n, empty family, n=1. It is not a restatement of the item and not a duplicate: lem-kun-0f11 is Z/n only, lem-etale-qcqs-finite-dimension-derived-coproducts and lem-exc-direct-image-coproducts need cd bounded for all modules, and the remaining candidates are proper or pro-etale. Nothing in the DAG states the item either (lem-kun-0f12 is absolute; lem-per-excellent-etale-constant-projection is Z/l^m ctf). No SGA is cited and this is not a re-split item. I accept the seven declared generic tool_uses. No changes.
